questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to protect your garden from animals like squirrels
Eating invasive species as a way to control them
Why lionfish are becoming endangered
The best seafood restaurants in Belize
questions.why: Phil says one of the simplest ways to deal with invasive species is just to eat them.

questions.q: What problem does Beth have in her garden?
options: Japanese knotweed is damaging the walls of her house
Her plants don't get enough light
Squirrels keep digging up what she plants
Insects are eating her vegetables
questions.why: She says every time she plants something, squirrels dig it up.

questions.q: How does Beth react when Phil suggests eating the squirrels?
options: She is surprised and can't quite believe it
She says she already does
She asks for a recipe
She gets angry with Phil and leaves the room
questions.why: She replies, “Sorry, what? Eat the squirrels?”

questions.q: What does the London restaurant Phil mentions offer?
options: Lionfish curry and other dishes from Belize
Only vegetarian food
Food from Japan
Squirrel kebabs and Japanese knotweed beer
questions.why: It offers squirrel kebabs, or you could try Japanese knotweed beer.

questions.q: According to Myra Anubi, why is Japanese knotweed so damaging?
options: It is poisonous to animals
It only grows near volcanoes, where it can survive the lava
It attracts invasive insects
Its strong roots kill other plants and damage buildings
questions.why: She says its roots can choke out surrounding plants and cause damage to buildings.

questions.q: What problem have lionfish caused in Belize?
options: They have attacked swimmers
They have harmed coral reefs and native wildlife
They have eaten all the squirrels
They have stopped local fishing boats from going out to sea
questions.why: Beth says they've had a massive impact on coral reefs and native wildlife.

questions.q: Why did the Belizean government ask famous chefs to cook lionfish?
options: To open new restaurants abroad
To win a cooking competition
To show lionfish is tasty and good for nature
To sell lionfish to other countries around the world
questions.why: It was to raise awareness that eating lionfish was both tasty and helping the environment.

questions.q: What did Celso Sho's organisation show fisheries and the public?
options: How to remove the spine so they can eat the fish
How to breed lionfish
How to cook squirrel
How to catch lionfish using special nets and traps
questions.why: He says they showed people how to remove the spine so they can eat the meat.
